spec.name: BeishaheBridge
spec.coordinateSystem: Local glTF axes: X transverse to bridge, Y up, Z along bridge from its north end toward its south end; origin at bridge center, sleeper top Y=0. X and Z are not geographic east and south until a placement transform is applied.
spec.reconstructionScope: Independent intact bridge candidate. Its 280 m length follows the present-day crossing/floodplain scale, not a proven 1938 bridge length. Fourteen 20 m spans, all member sections, the transverse timber deck and support layout, pier dimensions, deck elevation, damp staining, weathering and colors are authored design; none establishes the appearance or water level in March 1938. The 44 m compressed FirstLevel1218 blockout and legacy pontoon bridge are not replaced.

historicalReferences.image: JACAR C11111424100 appendix photo 12, 567 km bridge north of Tengxian
historicalReferences.supports: Nearby 1938 low pony truss silhouette, straight upper chord, inclined end posts, open above the track. Not identified as Beishahe itself.
Nearby short steel trusses, masonry support and demolition appearance. Not the Beishahe bridge.
User research archive; exact 1938 Beishahe bridge photograph still unconfirmed.

The modern Xianning bridge photograph in the user's archive is an out-of-region visual analogy for the central crossed braces and end-bay diagonals. The photograph's original attribution and date remain unverified; its members do not establish the Beishahe bridge's historical truss pattern.
1937 route description lists 1.435 m gauge and nominal 10 m, 41 kg/m rails for Tianjin-Xuzhou. Exact joint positions, rail section and bridge-specific fittings are not established.
1913 reference shows square-headed screw spikes with circular flanges for Prussian and Alsace-Lorraine railway track; an engineering analogy, not a photograph or specification of Beishahe.
1908 Minnesota road bridge: paired riveted members and gusset/floor-beam connections as an engineering analogy. Not a Chinese railway bridge, not evidence of Beishahe-specific details.

1941 Jinpu railway bridge at an unknown location: outside longitudinal timbers and a visible timber joint provide an engineering reference. Neither the dimensions nor their presence at Beishahe is established.

mapMeasurement.centerWgs84Role: Original map-query center, retained for compatibility; not the computed center of either mapped bridge.

illustrativeModernPlacement.originDefinition: Arithmetic mean of the four mapped endpoints; midway between two modern bridge axes, not the center of either individual bridge.
illustrativeModernPlacement.method: WGS84 ellipsoid ECEF projected to an east-north-up tangent plane at origin; average paired north endpoints and south endpoints before computing horizontal bearing.
illustrativeModernPlacement.conversion: east=0.760081535*x+0.649827716*z; north=0.649827716*x-0.760081535*z; up=y (all metres relative to the chosen origin and bridge-local vertical datum).
illustrativeModernPlacement.verticalDatum: Relative model Y=0 is sleeper top. Absolute elevation, bridge-deck height, and WGS84 ellipsoidal height are unknown.
illustrativeModernPlacement.limitations: Illustrative alignment to the midpoint between the modern twin bridges only; 280 m model support-axis length is not scaled to fit the 280.415 m mean axis. No 1938 bridge location, orientation, elevation, or original size is established.

modernWaterwaySketch.limitations: Coarse straight interpolation of adjacent modern OSM river-centerline nodes, not a surveyed channel or bank; angle and crossing are rough illustration only, with unquantified generalization error. They do not establish 1938 river alignment or conditions.

mapMeasurement.imagery: Esri World Imagery; OSM bridge endpoints checked against visible modern bridge ends
mapMeasurement.uncertainty: Modern mapped crossing includes floodplain. Water-channel estimate is image interpretation, approximately +/-5 to 10 m. Neither establishes the 1938 bank position or original bridge length. Model is deliberately rounded to 280 m.

materialInterpretation.trussBracing: Nine panels and three central counterbraced bays are an authored visual analogy to the modern Xianning bridge photograph in the user's archive, not evidence of the 1938 Beishahe truss. Bar sections, fasteners and face assignments are designed details.
materialInterpretation.trussFinish: Muted brown-gray weathered truss steel is an imagegen material study guided by a modern out-of-region bridge photograph. Its paint color and corrosion are creative choices, not verified 1938 Beishahe conditions. The rail body keeps a separate neutral steel texture.
materialInterpretation.pierDamp: A continuous pale brown-gray damp-to-dry transition on the lower pier courses is a creative weathering choice, not evidence of the 1938 waterline or site condition.
materialInterpretation.pierCap: Four individually jointed capstones with a solid inset base are an authored interpretation of an AI detail study, not evidence for the historic Beishahe pier cap.
materialInterpretation.deckPlanks: In response to the user's request for a complete deck, transverse planks were selected from the generated design study; presence and details are not established by a confirmed 1938 Beishahe bridge photograph.
materialInterpretation.jointTransitions: Rail and wooden deck splice details are authored to maintain a usable crossing; their exact construction is not established by a confirmed 1938 Beishahe bridge photograph.
materialInterpretation.railJoints: The 1937 route record gives nominal 10 m rails, while joint positions at midspan and supports, the 6 mm gaps, section dimensions and hardware are authored design assumptions. Represented through-bolt shafts overlap solid undrilled rail webs and plates.
materialInterpretation.railFasteners: Square-head screw-spike shape, 120 mm sleeper embed, two outside and one inside, and outside hook plates are authored interpretations of early German railway references, not established for the 1938 Beishahe bridge. Solid spike shafts intentionally overlap undrilled sleeper and tie-plate geometry; holes and threads are not modeled.
materialInterpretation.guardTimbers: Two low outer longitudinal timbers are an authored interpretation of a 1941 Jinpu railway bridge photograph at an unknown location; their use and dimensions at Beishahe are unconfirmed.

pierCap.interpretation: Authored construction; original Beishahe capstones are unconfirmed.

railJoints.interpretation: Spacing follows the 1937 Tianjin-Xuzhou line description; locations, joint gap, joint and rail sections are unverified design assumptions.

railFasteners.interpretation: Prussian-style screw-spike form, sleeper embed and axial tool envelope are authored analogies, not confirmed bridge-specific details.

guardTimbers.interpretation: Design inferred from an unidentified 1941 Jinpu railway bridge; not evidence for Beishahe's exact construction.
